questions.question: How can a company reduce its Total Cost of Ownership (TCO) using AWS?

explanation.summary: Minimizing upfront capital expenditures reduces TCO by leveraging AWS's pay-as-you-go and managed infrastructure models.
keyPoints: Shift from capital expenditure (CapEx) to operational expenditure (OpEx)
Avoids purchasing servers, storage, and networking hardware
Reduces facility and power costs associated with on-premises data centers
Leverages AWS managed services to lower infrastructure management overhead
Elastic scaling ensures payment aligns with actual usage
Cost predictability improves financial planning
Supports rapid experimentation without heavy upfront investment
examples: Launching EC2 instances instead of buying physical servers
Using RDS instead of setting up a full on-premises database environment
Storing data in S3 instead of building local storage arrays
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS enables organizations to reduce total IT costs by eliminating large upfront purchases, decreasing operational overhead, and providing flexible, scalable infrastructure. This principle is a core part of cloud economics and total cost of ownership calculations.

options.text: By having no responsibility for third-party license costs.

explanation.summary: AWS customers are still responsible for licensing costs unless using specific AWS License Included services.
explanation.why: Third-party software licensing is often the customer’s responsibility unless using AWS offerings with bundled licenses. AWS does not automatically cover all third-party software fees.

explanation.summary: Operational expenditures still exist; AWS reduces some operational overhead but does not eliminate all costs.
explanation.why: While AWS handles infrastructure management tasks, companies still pay for resource usage and manage applications, data, and users. OpEx is reduced, not removed.

explanation.summary: AWS manages infrastructure and services but customers manage their applications unless using fully managed PaaS services.
explanation.why: Application management, including code, configuration, and business logic, remains the customer's responsibility. Only services like AWS Lambda or managed databases offload operational tasks.

questions.question: Which options does AWS make available for customers who want to learn about security in the cloud in an instructor-led setting? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS Trusted Advisor provides automated checks and recommendations, not instructor-led training.
explanation.why: Trusted Advisor helps monitor AWS accounts but is not a learning platform or instructor-led course.

explanation.summary: AWS Online Tech Talks are live and on-demand sessions, often instructor-led or hosted by AWS experts, covering security topics among others.
keyPoints: Webinars and tech talks hosted by AWS experts
Covers cloud security best practices, compliance, and architecture
Accessible online for remote learning
Includes Q&A for interactive learning
Often instructor-led or guided
examples: AWS Security Fundamentals tech talk
Webinar on securing multi-account AWS environments
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS offers multiple formats for learning security, including classroom training, online tech talks, and self-paced courses. Online Tech Talks are a flexible way to learn security practices with guidance from AWS instructors.

explanation.summary: AWS Blog posts provide information but are not instructor-led training.
explanation.why: Blogs are self-paced reading resources, not structured instructor-led learning sessions.

explanation.summary: AWS Forums are community discussion platforms, not instructor-led classes.
explanation.why: Forums facilitate peer discussion and Q&A, not structured classroom instruction.

explanation.summary: AWS Classroom Training provides in-person or virtual instructor-led sessions, including cloud security topics.
keyPoints: Instructor-led courses with structured curriculum
Covers AWS security, architecture, and compliance
Hands-on labs and exercises included
Certificates of completion available
examples: AWS Security Essentials course
AWS Architecting on AWS classroom course with security modules
explanation.additionalInfo: Classroom training is designed for formal, interactive learning with AWS-certified instructors. It’s the primary method AWS provides instructor-led education for security.

questions.question: Which of the following will enhance the security of access to the AWS Management Console? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: Secrets Manager is used for managing secrets like database credentials, not for console login security.
explanation.why: While useful for credentials management, Secrets Manager does not enhance the security of AWS Management Console access directly.

explanation.summary: Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates, which do not directly secure console login.
explanation.why: SSL/TLS certificates secure endpoints for services but do not control AWS console authentication.

explanation.summary: AWS MFA adds a second authentication factor to console logins, greatly enhancing security.
keyPoints: Requires users to provide a one-time code in addition to password
Supports virtual, hardware, or SMS MFA devices
Protects against compromised passwords
Recommended best practice for privileged users
Enforces additional layer in shared responsibility model
examples: A root user requires MFA to log in
Administrators enabled virtual MFA apps like Google Authenticator for console access
explanation.additionalInfo: MFA is considered a fundamental security control for AWS accounts, reducing risk of unauthorized access even if passwords are compromised.

explanation.summary: Security groups control network traffic to resources, not console access.
explanation.why: They do not affect login authentication for the AWS Management Console.

explanation.summary: Password policies enforce strong password requirements for IAM users, enhancing console security.
keyPoints: Set minimum password length and complexity
Enforce password rotation
Prevent reuse of previous passwords
Ensure IAM users follow best practices
Part of shared responsibility model
examples: Require administrators to use 12-character complex passwords
Enforce password change every 90 days for IAM users
explanation.additionalInfo: Configuring password policies is a standard security measure to strengthen AWS Management Console access. Combined with MFA, it significantly reduces the risk of account compromise.

questions.question: Which of the following features can be configured through the Amazon Virtual Private Cloud (Amazon VPC) Dashboard? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: CloudFront distributions are managed in the CloudFront console, not in the VPC dashboard.
explanation.why: VPC dashboard manages network resources like subnets, route tables, and security groups, not CDN services.

explanation.summary: Route 53 is a DNS service and is configured in its own console, not through the VPC dashboard.
explanation.why: VPC dashboard does not manage DNS hosted zones or routing policies provided by Route 53.

explanation.summary: Security Groups are configurable through the VPC dashboard, controlling inbound and outbound traffic for resources within the VPC.
keyPoints: Define inbound and outbound traffic rules
Associated with EC2 instances and other resources
Acts as a virtual firewall at the instance level
Can be applied to multiple instances
Supports both TCP, UDP, and ICMP protocols
examples: Allow port 443 inbound for web servers
Restrict SSH access to specific IP ranges
explanation.additionalInfo: Security Groups are fundamental VPC network controls and are fully managed within the VPC dashboard. They operate at the instance level, providing a stateful firewall mechanism that automatically allows response traffic for allowed inbound connections.

explanation.summary: Subnets are configured within a VPC to partition the IP address space and organize resources.
keyPoints: Define IP ranges within a VPC
Organize resources into logical network segments
Supports public and private access control
Works with route tables and gateways
Enables isolation and segmentation
examples: Create a public subnet for web servers with internet access
Create a private subnet for database instances
explanation.additionalInfo: Subnets are core elements of VPC design, enabling the separation of workloads based on security, access, and operational requirements. They can span Availability Zones to enhance availability and resilience.

explanation.summary: Load balancers are managed separately via the Elastic Load Balancing console, not the VPC dashboard.
explanation.why: VPC dashboard is for networking constructs like subnets and security groups; ELB configuration is done in its dedicated console.

questions.question: For which auditing process does AWS have sole responsibility?

explanation.summary: IAM policies are customer-managed and are the responsibility of the user.
explanation.why: Customers configure IAM policies to control access; AWS does not manage or enforce individual policy definitions.

explanation.summary: AWS is solely responsible for the physical security of its data centers.
keyPoints: Controls access to data center facilities
Manages surveillance and security staff
Implements environmental controls
Maintains hardware integrity and disaster protections
Responsible for compliance with physical security standards
examples: Secure access via biometric authentication
CCTV monitoring and restricted zones within AWS data centers
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the AWS shared responsibility model, AWS is fully responsible for the physical security of the infrastructure. Customers focus on security in the cloud, including data, identity, and access management.

explanation.summary: S3 bucket policies are customer-managed configurations.
explanation.why: Users define S3 access policies; AWS does not manage individual bucket permissions.

explanation.summary: CloudTrail logs are customer-managed for auditing purposes.
explanation.why: Customers enable and configure CloudTrail; AWS provides the service but does not manage the content of each account’s logs.

questions.question: Which of the following are advantages of AWS consolidated billing? (Select TWO)

options.text: The ability to receive one bill for multiple accounts.

explanation.summary: Consolidated billing allows a payer account to receive a single invoice for all linked accounts.
keyPoints: Simplifies financial management across multiple accounts
Aggregates charges for easier reconciliation
Reduces administrative overhead
Supports centralized budgeting and reporting
Enables unified tracking of usage costs
examples: Parent company receiving one invoice for all subsidiaries
Simplifying monthly cost reporting for multiple projects
explanation.additionalInfo: Consolidated billing is an AWS Organizations feature that helps reduce billing complexity and improve cost visibility for multi-account environments.

options.text: Service limits increasing by default in all accounts.

explanation.summary: Service limits are set per account and are not increased automatically through consolidated billing.
explanation.why: Consolidated billing does not change AWS service quotas or limits.

options.text: A fixed discount on the monthly bill.

explanation.summary: AWS does not provide a fixed discount; cost savings depend on aggregated usage.
explanation.why: Consolidated billing may lead to volume discounts but not fixed discounts.

options.text: Potential volume discounts, as usage in all accounts is combined.

explanation.summary: Aggregating usage across accounts can lead to volume-based pricing benefits.
keyPoints: Combined usage may reach thresholds for lower pricing tiers
Optimizes cost efficiency for multiple accounts
Reduces per-unit costs when usage aggregates across accounts
Supports budgeting and forecasting
examples: Multiple departments share a single billing account and benefit from tiered S3 pricing
Combined EC2 usage may reduce cost per instance for large-scale deployments
explanation.additionalInfo: Consolidated billing allows organizations to maximize volume discounts and cost efficiency by combining all account usage into a single calculation.

options.text: The automatic extension of the master account’s AWS support plan to all accounts.

explanation.summary: Support plans must be selected per account; consolidated billing does not automatically extend support.
explanation.why: Master account’s support plan does not propagate to linked accounts. Each account chooses its own plan.

questions.question: Which of the following common IT tasks can AWS cover to free up company IT resources? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: AWS handles patching of managed database services, reducing operational overhead.
keyPoints: Automates OS and database engine patching
Reduces downtime risk and maintenance effort
Supports point-in-time recovery during updates
Maintains security compliance with latest updates
Applicable for RDS, Aurora, and other managed databases
examples: AWS automatically applies security patches to RDS instances
Managed Aurora clusters updated without manual intervention
explanation.additionalInfo: By offloading patch management to AWS, companies can focus on application logic and business processes rather than routine maintenance tasks.

explanation.summary: Testing applications is still a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS provides infrastructure but customers design and execute test plans for their software deployments.

explanation.summary: AWS automatically manages backups for managed databases like RDS, including point-in-time recovery.
keyPoints: Supports automated daily backups
Manual snapshots available for specific times
Reduces operational overhead for customers
Stored securely in Amazon S3
Supports retention policies and compliance
examples: RDS automated backup with 7-day retention
Manual snapshot before major schema update
explanation.additionalInfo: Database backups are integral to managed services. Automating this task frees IT teams from scheduling, monitoring, and maintaining backup routines.

explanation.summary: Schema creation remains the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS manages infrastructure and backups, but database design and schema definition must be handled by users.

explanation.summary: Security testing is a customer responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS provides infrastructure, but customers must plan and execute security assessments per policy.

questions.question: A company wants to expand from one AWS Region into a second AWS Region. What does the company need to do to start supporting the new Region?

options.text: Contact an AWS Account Manager to sign a new contract.

explanation.summary: No new contract is required to deploy in additional AWS Regions.
explanation.why: All AWS Regions are accessible under the existing account. Deployment decisions and resource creation are sufficient.

options.text: Move an Availability Zone to the new Region.

explanation.summary: Availability Zones are fixed physical locations and cannot be moved.
explanation.why: AZs are managed by AWS; customers deploy resources in existing AZs within the chosen Region.

options.text: Begin deploying resources in the second Region.

explanation.summary: Customers can start using a new AWS Region by deploying resources there.
keyPoints: No additional contracts required
Resources are independent per Region
Enables geographic distribution for latency and compliance
Can replicate applications and data as needed
Supports disaster recovery and failover
examples: Launch EC2 instances in the new Region for expansion
Deploy RDS instances in multiple Regions for redundancy
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Regions provide isolated infrastructure. Expanding to a new Region involves provisioning resources there; data and application replication are managed by customer decisions.

options.text: Download the AWS Management Console for the new Region.

explanation.summary: The AWS Management Console is web-based and works across all Regions; no download is required.
explanation.why: Users access the same console and select the desired Region from the interface.

questions.question: Why is it beneficial to use Elastic Load Balancers with applications?

options.text: They allow for the conversion from Application Load.

explanation.summary: This is incorrect and incomplete; ELB does not convert load balancer types automatically.
explanation.why: Elastic Load Balancing distributes incoming traffic but does not perform type conversions on its own.

explanation.summary: Classic Load Balancer is one type of ELB; this does not explain the benefit.
explanation.why: The main benefit is traffic distribution and handling variable network loads, not conversion between balancer types.

options.text: They are capable of handling constant changes in network traffic patterns.

explanation.summary: ELBs automatically distribute traffic across multiple instances, adapting to changing loads.
keyPoints: Distribute incoming requests to healthy instances
Automatically scale to meet varying traffic demands
Provide high availability and fault tolerance
Supports multiple protocols (HTTP, HTTPS, TCP)
examples: Web applications with fluctuating daily traffic patterns
Auto-scaling EC2 fleet behind an Application Load Balancer
explanation.additionalInfo: ELBs improve application resilience and responsiveness by dynamically adjusting to traffic changes, ensuring consistent performance and uptime.

options.text: They automatically adjust capacity. They are provided at no charge to users.

explanation.summary: ELB does adjust traffic distribution but is a paid service; capacity adjustment is not free.
explanation.why: Charges apply based on usage; automatic scaling improves traffic handling but incurs cost.

questions.question: Which is the MINIMUM AWS Support plan that allows for one-hour target response time for support cases?

explanation.summary: Enterprise plan offers faster response times but is not the minimum plan for 1-hour response.
explanation.why: Business Support provides 1-hour response time for urgent production issues at lower cost than Enterprise.

explanation.summary: Business Support plan provides a 1-hour response target for urgent production system issues.
keyPoints: Supports 24/7 access via phone, email, and chat
1-hour response for production system impaired cases
Includes support for third-party software and guidance
Access to AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Lower cost than Enterprise Support for mid-tier response
examples: Production website outage with urgent resolution needed
Critical RDS service issue requiring immediate attention
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Business Support is designed for customers who need faster response times than Developer Support but may not require the dedicated concierge features of Enterprise Support.

explanation.summary: Developer Support does not guarantee 1-hour response times.
explanation.why: Developer plan targets best-effort response for non-production issues, typically slower than 1 hour.

explanation.summary: Basic Support offers only limited self-service support.
explanation.why: It does not provide any guaranteed response times or 24/7 access to support engineers.

questions.question: What is the lowest-cost, durable storage option for retaining database backups for immediate retrieval?

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 offers durable, immediately accessible storage at low cost suitable for database backups.
keyPoints: Highly durable with 11 nines of durability
Immediate retrieval of stored data
Cost-effective compared to other options for frequently accessed backups
Supports versioning and lifecycle policies
Integrates with AWS backup solutions
examples: Storing RDS snapshots in S3 for compliance and recovery
Backing up application databases for quick restore
explanation.additionalInfo: S3 provides a combination of durability, availability, and cost efficiency, making it ideal for backups requiring frequent or immediate access. Glacier is cheaper but designed for archival with retrieval delays.

explanation.summary: Glacier is designed for long-term archival, not immediate retrieval.
explanation.why: Retrieval times can range from minutes to hours, making it unsuitable for immediate backup access.

explanation.summary: EBS is block storage for EC2 instances, not ideal for long-term backup retention at low cost.
explanation.why: While durable and attached to instances, EBS volumes incur higher costs for backup storage compared to S3.

explanation.summary: Instance Store is ephemeral storage that is lost when the instance stops.
explanation.why: It cannot be relied upon for durable database backups.

questions.question: What AWS team assists customers with accelerating cloud adoption through paid engagements in any of several specialty practice areas?

explanation.summary: Enterprise Support provides technical guidance but does not deliver specialized paid consulting engagements.
explanation.why: Professional Services team is responsible for specialty engagements to accelerate adoption.

explanation.summary: Solutions Architects provide guidance but are not the paid engagement team.
explanation.why: They assist in architectural design but consulting engagements are handled by Professional Services.

explanation.summary: AWS Professional Services delivers paid, specialized engagements to accelerate cloud adoption.
keyPoints: Provides expert consulting across multiple domains
Helps design, implement, and optimize AWS solutions
Assists with migration and adoption strategies
Supports compliance, security, and operational best practices
Paid engagements customized to customer needs
examples: Engaging Professional Services to migrate a large enterprise data center
Cloud adoption workshops for optimizing architecture and costs
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Professional Services is the dedicated team for customers requiring hands-on, paid assistance to accelerate AWS adoption and achieve business outcomes quickly.

explanation.summary: Account Managers provide customer relationship support but do not perform technical engagements.
explanation.why: They handle business account guidance, not specialized technical consulting.

questions.question: A company needs 24/7 phone, email, and chat access with a response time of less than 1 hour if a production system has a service interruption. Which AWS Support plan meets these requirements at the LOWEST cost?

explanation.summary: Basic support provides only limited self-service resources without guaranteed 1-hour response.
explanation.why: Basic does not provide 24/7 access to support engineers or SLA-based response times.

explanation.summary: Developer support is aimed at non-production use and does not guarantee 1-hour response.
explanation.why: Developer plan has best-effort support and longer response times.

explanation.summary: Business Support provides 24/7 access and 1-hour response for urgent production system issues at the lowest cost for these requirements.
keyPoints: 24/7 access via phone, chat, and email
1-hour response for production system impaired cases
Includes guidance for third-party software issues
Access to AWS Trusted Advisor checks
Cost-effective compared to Enterprise for mid-tier response needs
examples: Urgent RDS outage requiring immediate support
Production EC2 failure requiring prompt resolution
explanation.additionalInfo: Business Support is the recommended minimum plan for production workloads that require rapid response to critical system issues.

explanation.summary: Enterprise Support provides faster and more personalized services but is not the lowest-cost option for 1-hour response.
explanation.why: Enterprise includes concierge services and technical account managers, increasing cost above the minimum needed.

questions.question: If a customer needs to audit the change management of AWS resources, which of the following AWS services should the customer use?

explanation.summary: AWS Config records and tracks configuration changes of AWS resources, enabling auditing and compliance.
keyPoints: Monitors and records resource configurations
Tracks changes over time
Provides audit trails for compliance
Supports automated compliance evaluation
Integrates with CloudTrail for enhanced auditing
examples: Track security group changes over time
Validate configuration compliance for EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: AWS Config is designed specifically to enable governance, compliance, and risk management by providing a history of AWS resource configurations and changes.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not detailed change auditing.
explanation.why: It identifies potential cost, performance, or security issues but does not log all configuration changes.

explanation.summary: CloudWatch monitors metrics and logs, not detailed configuration change history.
explanation.why: While useful for operational insights, CloudWatch is not a change management audit tool.

explanation.summary: Inspector performs security assessments, not configuration change auditing.
explanation.why: It identifies vulnerabilities but does not track resource changes over time.

questions.question: How does AWS Trusted Advisor provide guidance to users of the AWS Cloud? (Select TWO)

options.text: It identifies software vulnerabilities in applications running on AWS.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not analyze application code for vulnerabilities.
explanation.why: It evaluates AWS account configurations, not application-level software vulnerabilities.

options.text: It provides a list of cost optimization recommendations based on current AWS usage.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor analyzes usage patterns to suggest ways to reduce costs.
keyPoints: Identifies idle or underutilized resources
Suggests reserved instance purchases for cost savings
Provides guidance on deleting unused snapshots or volumes
Monitors service limits to prevent over-provisioning
examples: Notifying customer of unused EC2 instances that could be terminated
Recommending S3 storage optimization
explanation.additionalInfo: Cost optimization is one of Trusted Advisor’s primary pillars, helping customers manage AWS costs effectively.

options.text: It detects potential security vulnerabilities caused by permissions settings on account resources.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor evaluates security best practices, including IAM and S3 permissions, to identify risks.
keyPoints: Checks for overly permissive IAM policies
Identifies publicly accessible S3 buckets
Highlights security gaps in configurations
Provides actionable recommendations to mitigate risk
examples: Alerting if an S3 bucket is publicly accessible
Recommending least privilege access for IAM users
explanation.additionalInfo: Security checks are an integral part of Trusted Advisor to ensure AWS accounts follow best practices and minimize exposure to threats.

options.text: It automatically corrects potential security issues caused by permissions settings on account resources.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides recommendations but does not automatically fix security issues.
explanation.why: Customers must manually apply changes to correct identified security risks.

options.text: It provides proactive alerting whenever an Amazon EC2 instance has been compromised.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor does not provide active intrusion detection or monitoring of EC2 instances.
explanation.why: Security alerts for compromised instances are handled by services like GuardDuty or CloudWatch, not Trusted Advisor.

questions.question: Which AWS managed service is used to host databases?

explanation.summary: AWS Batch is for batch computing workloads, not database hosting.
explanation.why: It manages compute resources for batch jobs rather than providing managed database services.

explanation.summary: AWS Artifact provides access to compliance reports and agreements, not database hosting.
explanation.why: It does not offer managed database services or instances.

explanation.summary: AWS Data Pipeline orchestrates data workflows but does not host databases.
explanation.why: It moves and transforms data, but persistent database hosting is not its purpose.

explanation.summary: Amazon RDS is a managed relational database service that hosts database instances in AWS.
keyPoints: Supports multiple database engines (MySQL, PostgreSQL, Oracle, SQL Server, Aurora)
Automates backups, patching, and replication
Scales compute and storage independently
Provides multi-AZ deployment for high availability
Fully managed by AWS, reducing operational overhead
examples: Launching an RDS MySQL instance for a web application
Using RDS PostgreSQL with automated backups and snapshots
explanation.additionalInfo: Amazon RDS simplifies database administration by handling routine tasks, enabling developers to focus on application development and scaling without managing underlying infrastructure.

questions.question: Which of the following Identity and Access Management (IAM) entities is associated with an access key ID and secret access key when using AWS Command Line Interface (AWS CLI)?

explanation.summary: IAM groups are collections of users for permission management, not individual credentials.
explanation.why: Access keys are assigned to users, not groups.

explanation.summary: IAM users are assigned access keys that allow programmatic access via AWS CLI or SDKs.
keyPoints: Users can have long-term access key ID and secret access key
Enable CLI, SDK, and API access
Credentials can be rotated and revoked
IAM users inherit permissions from policies attached to user or group
Essential for automation and programmatic access
examples: A developer creates an IAM user and assigns an access key to run automation scripts via CLI
Automated deployment pipelines using IAM user credentials
explanation.additionalInfo: IAM users are the primary entity for programmatic access to AWS. Best practices recommend using IAM roles where possible, but access keys are directly tied to IAM users for CLI and SDK access.

explanation.summary: IAM roles are assumed by entities and do not have long-term access keys directly.
explanation.why: Roles provide temporary credentials via STS, not static access key ID and secret key.

explanation.summary: Policies define permissions, not credentials.
explanation.why: Access keys are associated with users, not policies.

questions.question: Under the shared responsibility model, which of the following is the customer responsible for?

options.text: Ensuring network connectivity from AWS to the internet.

explanation.summary: AWS manages network connectivity from its services to the internet.
explanation.why: Customers configure network security but not the underlying connectivity of AWS infrastructure.

options.text: Patching and fixing flaws within the AWS Cloud infrastructure.

explanation.summary: AWS is responsible for patching its infrastructure.
explanation.why: Customers focus on patching their applications and OS within EC2 or managed services.

options.text: Ensuring the physical security of cloud data centers.

explanation.summary: Physical security is solely AWS’s responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage data center access, surveillance, or environmental controls.

options.text: Ensuring Amazon EBS volumes are backed up.

explanation.summary: Customers are responsible for managing data backups of their EBS volumes.
keyPoints: Automated snapshots must be configured by customer
Data retention policies controlled by customer
Ensures recovery and compliance requirements are met
AWS provides snapshot functionality but customer triggers and manages backups
Applies to EC2 instances and EBS volumes
examples: Creating scheduled EBS snapshots via AWS Backup
Manually triggering snapshots before critical updates
explanation.additionalInfo: Under the shared responsibility model, AWS manages infrastructure and physical security while customers manage their data, including EBS backup strategies.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides a simple and scalable shared file storage solution for use with Linux-based AWS and on-premises servers?

explanation.summary: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a shared file system for Linux servers.
explanation.why: S3 provides key-value object storage accessible via APIs, not POSIX-compliant file system mounts.

explanation.summary: Glacier is archival storage, not a shared file system.
explanation.why: Glacier is optimized for long-term storage with retrieval delays, unsuitable for live Linux file sharing.

explanation.summary: EBS provides block storage attached to single EC2 instances, not a shared file system.
explanation.why: EBS volumes cannot be concurrently mounted across multiple Linux servers for shared access.

explanation.summary: Amazon EFS provides a scalable, fully managed shared file system for Linux-based instances and on-premises servers.
keyPoints: POSIX-compliant file system accessible by multiple instances
Elastic scaling with storage automatically adjusting to usage
Supports NFSv4 protocol
Can be accessed concurrently from multiple EC2 instances or on-premises servers
Ideal for content management, home directories, and big data workflows
examples: Shared home directories for Linux servers
Storing media assets for web applications across multiple EC2 instances
explanation.additionalInfo: EFS allows customers to create scalable, durable, and highly available shared file storage accessible across multiple compute resources without provisioning or managing file servers.

questions.question: What credential components are required to gain programmatic access to an AWS account? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: The access key ID is part of the credentials needed for programmatic API, CLI, and SDK access.
keyPoints: Used with the secret access key to authenticate requests
Associated with IAM users or roles
Required for CLI and SDK usage
Can be rotated and deactivated for security
Essential for automation scripts and applications
examples: Configuring AWS CLI with aws_access_key_id and aws_secret_access_key
Programmatically uploading objects to S3 using access keys
explanation.additionalInfo: Access keys grant secure programmatic access without using passwords, and must be managed according to best practices to avoid compromise.

explanation.summary: Primary keys are database concepts, not AWS account credentials.
explanation.why: They are unrelated to programmatic access to AWS resources.

explanation.summary: The secret access key is used alongside the access key ID to authenticate API requests.
keyPoints: Works in combination with access key ID
Used for signing AWS API requests
Sensitive and should not be shared publicly
Can be rotated periodically
Required for programmatic access via CLI, SDK, or API
examples: AWS CLI command using aws_secret_access_key
SDK applications authenticating to AWS services
explanation.additionalInfo: Managing secret access keys securely is critical to prevent unauthorized access. AWS recommends using IAM roles where possible to avoid long-term static keys.

explanation.summary: A user ID alone is not sufficient for programmatic access.
explanation.why: Access requires credentials like access key ID and secret access key, not just the IAM user name.

explanation.summary: AWS does not require a secondary key for programmatic access.
explanation.why: Only the access key ID and secret access key pair are necessary.

questions.question: Which of the following is a shared control between the customer and AWS?

options.text: Providing a key for Amazon S3 client-side encryption.

explanation.summary: S3 client-side encryption is fully managed by the customer.
explanation.why: AWS provides the service but does not manage the keys or encryption for customer-side encrypted data.

options.text: Configuration of an Amazon EC2 instance.

explanation.summary: EC2 instance configuration is the customer’s responsibility.
explanation.why: AWS provides the underlying infrastructure but customers configure OS, software, and security settings.

options.text: Environmental controls of physical AWS data centers.

explanation.summary: Physical environmental controls are fully AWS’s responsibility.
explanation.why: Customers do not manage power, cooling, or physical security in AWS data centers.

explanation.summary: Awareness is a shared control where AWS provides training and documentation, and the customer implements best practices.
keyPoints: AWS provides tools, guides, and best-practice recommendations
Customers must implement policies and procedures accordingly
Shared responsibility for security awareness, compliance, and governance
Includes training, auditing, and monitoring responsibilities
examples: Customer follows AWS security best practices for IAM
AWS provides guidance on account management and compliance
explanation.additionalInfo: Awareness represents a shared control under the AWS shared responsibility model where both parties must actively participate to maintain security and compliance.

questions.question: Which type of AWS storage is ephemeral and is deleted when an instance is stopped or terminated?

explanation.summary: EBS provides persistent block storage that survives instance stops.
explanation.why: Data on EBS volumes remains until explicitly deleted, unlike ephemeral instance store.

explanation.summary: Instance store provides ephemeral storage tied to the lifecycle of an EC2 instance.
keyPoints: Deleted when instance stops or terminates
Provides temporary block-level storage
High IOPS for temporary data
Not suitable for persistent backups
Used for caching, buffer, or scratch data
examples: Temporary web server cache
Scratch space for data processing jobs
explanation.additionalInfo: Ephemeral instance store is ideal for temporary storage needs where persistence is not required. For durable storage, EBS or S3 should be used.

explanation.summary: EFS provides durable, shared file storage and is not ephemeral.
explanation.why: Data persists across instance terminations and is accessible concurrently.

explanation.summary: S3 is object storage, fully durable and persistent.
explanation.why: Data in S3 is not tied to the lifecycle of EC2 instances.

questions.question: Which of the following is an advantage of consolidated billing on AWS?

questions.question: Which services are parts of the AWS serverless platform?

options.text: Amazon Athena, Amazon Cognito, Amazon EC2.

explanation.summary: EC2 is not serverless, so this combination is incorrect.

questions.question: Which of the following Amazon EC2 pricing models allow customers to use existing server-bound software licenses?

questions.question: Which of the following security measures protect access to an AWS account? (Select TWO)

options.text: Grant least privilege access to IAM users.

Limits impact of compromised credentials
Reduces attack surface in AWS account
Encourages adherence to security best practices
Integral to IAM security management

Admin rights granted only to operations team

questions.question: Which AWS service provides the ability to manage infrastructure as code?

questions.question: What is an advantage of deploying an application across multiple Availability Zones?

options.text: There is a lower risk of service failure if a natural disaster causes a service disruption in a given AWS Region.

Reduces risk of downtime due to hardware or network failures

Web servers distributed across AZs behind an ELB

options.text: There will be better coverage as Availability Zones are geographically distant and can serve a wider area.

explanation.why: Multi-AZ ensures availability, not geographic reach.

options.text: There will be decreased application latency that will improve the user experience.

explanation.summary: Multi-AZ deployment does not inherently reduce latency; it primarily provides high availability.

questions.question: A customer needs to run a MySQL database that easily scales. Which AWS service should they use?

questions.question: Which of the following is an AWS Cloud architecture design principle?

explanation.summary: Vertical scaling alone is not a recommended cloud architecture principle.

questions.question: A company will be moving from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. What would be one financial difference after the move?

options.text: Moving from variable operational expense (OpEx) to upfront capital expense (CapEx).

options.text: Moving from upfront capital expense (CapEx) to variable capital expense (CapEx).

questions.question: Which AWS service should be used for long-term, low-cost storage of data backups?

examples: Storing European customer data in AWS EU (Frankfurt) region
Ensuring sensitive financial data remains within required jurisdictions
explanation.additionalInfo: Data sovereignty is an important consideration for organizations handling sensitive or regulated data, influencing the choice of AWS Region.

explanation.summary: AWS manages cooling and operational costs internally; this is not a customer decision factor.
explanation.why: Customers do not choose regions based on data center cooling costs.

options.text: Proximity to the customer’s office for on-site visits.

explanation.summary: AWS regions are globally managed and do not require physical visits from the customer.
explanation.why: Operational interaction with AWS data centers is not needed for region selection.

questions.question: Which AWS service provides alerts when an AWS event may impact a company’s AWS resources?

explanation.summary: Personal Health Dashboard delivers proactive notifications and guidance for events affecting a customer’s resources.
keyPoints: Customized view of AWS service health for the account
Alerts for planned maintenance and unplanned events
Provides remediation guidance
Supports automated responses through CloudWatch Events
Helps maintain operational continuity and SLA adherence
examples: Notification of RDS maintenance affecting production databases
Alert for EC2 instance status changes impacting applications
explanation.additionalInfo: Personal Health Dashboard enables organizations to respond quickly to events that could impact their workloads, unlike the general Service Health Dashboard.

explanation.summary: Service Health Dashboard provides general AWS service status, not customer-specific alerts.
explanation.why: It shows global service information, not tailored to a customer’s resources.

explanation.summary: Trusted Advisor provides best-practice recommendations, not real-time alerts for AWS events.
explanation.why: It focuses on cost optimization, performance, and security checks rather than event notifications.

explanation.summary: Infrastructure Event Management is a professional service engagement, not an automated alerting system.
explanation.why: It involves consultation for planned events, not automatic notifications for account-specific events.

questions.question: Which disaster recovery scenario offers the lowest probability of downtime?

explanation.summary: Backup and restore has higher downtime because restoration can take hours to days.
explanation.why: It involves recovering from backups, not maintaining an active standby environment.

explanation.summary: Pilot light reduces downtime compared to backup/restore but still requires startup time for the environment.
explanation.why: Some services need to be provisioned or scaled up when an outage occurs.

explanation.summary: Warm standby provides pre-provisioned but scaled-down resources, reducing downtime but not eliminating it.
explanation.why: Some scaling and activation are required upon failure.

explanation.summary: Multi-site active-active provides the highest availability and lowest downtime by running workloads simultaneously in multiple locations.
keyPoints: Workloads run concurrently across multiple regions or data centers
Automatic failover with minimal or no downtime
Supports high SLA requirements
Ensures business continuity even during large-scale outages
Reduces recovery point and recovery time objectives to near zero
examples: Active-active deployment of web servers and databases in US East and EU West
Global applications maintaining uptime during regional disasters
explanation.additionalInfo: Active-active architectures are the preferred disaster recovery approach for mission-critical applications requiring near-zero downtime and high availability.

questions.question: Which service’s PRIMARY purpose is software version control?

explanation.summary: CodeStar is a project management service that integrates CI/CD, not dedicated to version control.
explanation.why: Version control is handled by CodeCommit within CodeStar projects, not CodeStar itself.

explanation.summary: AWS CLI is a tool for interacting with AWS services programmatically, not for version control.
explanation.why: It does not track software changes or repositories.

explanation.summary: Cognito provides authentication and user management, not version control.
explanation.why: It handles identity management, not code repositories.

explanation.summary: AWS CodeCommit is a fully managed source control service for hosting Git-based repositories.
keyPoints: Supports Git commands and workflows
Provides secure, scalable, and highly available repositories
Integrates with CI/CD pipelines and other AWS DevOps tools
Reduces operational overhead compared to self-managed Git servers
Supports fine-grained access control
examples: Hosting application source code for automated deployment
Collaborative development with teams using CodeCommit repositories
explanation.additionalInfo: CodeCommit allows developers to maintain version control, track changes, and collaborate without managing underlying infrastructure.

questions.question: How can a customer increase security to AWS account logons? (Select TWO)

explanation.summary: Certificate Manager manages SSL/TLS certificates, not user authentication.
explanation.why: It does not directly enhance AWS account logon security.

explanation.summary: MFA adds a second authentication factor, significantly improving account security.
keyPoints: Requires password and time-based one-time code
Reduces risk of unauthorized access even if credentials are compromised
Supports virtual, hardware, or SMS MFA devices
Recommended for root and privileged IAM users
Part of shared responsibility model
examples: Root account login requires MFA token
Developers using virtual MFA apps like Google Authenticator
explanation.additionalInfo: Activating MFA is a best practice to enhance AWS account login security and is highly recommended by AWS.

options.text: Use Amazon Cognito to manage access

explanation.summary: Cognito manages user identities for applications, not IAM console access.
explanation.why: It is used for application-level authentication, not AWS account login security.

explanation.summary: Strong password policies enforce complexity and rotation, improving logon security.
keyPoints: Set minimum password length and complexity
Enforce password rotation and prevent reuse
Reduces risk of account compromise
Applies to IAM users and root account
Integral part of shared responsibility model
examples: Enforcing 12-character complex passwords for administrators
Mandating 90-day rotation for IAM user passwords
explanation.additionalInfo: Combining strong password policies with MFA provides a layered approach to securing AWS account logons.

explanation.summary: Organizations manages multiple accounts and permissions; it does not directly enforce stronger logon security.
explanation.why: While helpful for centralized management, it does not replace MFA or password policies.
